summary_md: **Liqin Ye ([@liqinye27](https://x.com/liqinye27/status/2115210517425934505))** introduces **Forecast-Dojo**, a replayable environment for benchmarking and training LLM forecasting agents on rewound real-world events without hindsight. The thread reports research tools improve all 12 evaluated models, memory notebooks cut API cost by a median 24% with trade-offs, and trajectories from the dojo fine-tune a Qwen3-30B-A3B model into a better forecaster; paper, site, code and data linked.

Forecast Dojo — A time machine for forecasting agents.

relevance: A training/eval environment for agents reasoning under evolving evidence.

media.description: Animated GIF introducing Forecast-Dojo, the replayable forecasting environment (not downloaded; referenced only).

Forecast-Dojo overview: 1,568 Polymarket events (1,338 train, 230 eval) and 18.8M dated CC-News articles; each question is forecast repeatedly over a temporally evolving corpus by an LLM agent with search/read/compute tools, a sandbox and an optional notebook memory, scored by Brier and usable for SFT, RL or on-policy distillation.

Scatter plots of Brier score vs accuracy for memory-free and memory-on forecasting agents (GPT-5.6 Sol, GPT-5.5, GPT-5.4, Opus 4.8/4.6, GLM-5, Kimi K2.5, Qwen3.5-397B, DeepSeek-V3.2, MiniMax M2.5, Nemotron 3 Super, gpt-oss-120b), all trailing the market reference at ~65% accuracy and ~0.50 Brier.

Three panels: Brier improving across forecast step position for memory-free and memory-on agents versus no-tools and market; Brier change by quartile of new evidence; and Brier improvement correlating with evidence capture κ across proprietary and open-weight models (ρ = 0.74).

Cost and tool-use charts: USD per forecast for GPT-5.6 Sol, 5.5, 5.4 and Claude Opus 4.8/4.6 with no tools, memory-free and memory-on (about $0.18–$5.85), and research calls per forecast split into search, read and Python, from GPT-5.6 Sol (136.6 memory-free) down to MiniMax M2.5 (12.5 memory-on).
